categories.name: PWM Timer and PA8 Output Driver
categories.description: Covers PWM timer setup, PA8/D7 pin routing, carrier-frequency configuration, output semantics, startup sequencing, and initialization-failure behavior.
requirements: The firmware shall start PWM generation automatically after board initialization.
The firmware shall output a PWM signal on the Arduino D7 pin (CN9 pin 8 / MCU pin PA8).
PA8 shall be configured in a supported timer alternate-function PWM output mode.
The PWM carrier frequency shall remain constant while the duty cycle changes.
The default PWM carrier frequency shall be 1 kHz.
The PWM output shall be interpreted as duty-cycle modulation of a 3.3 V MCU logic output on D7, not as a variable 5 V supply rail.
The D7/PA8 output shall remain in a defined inactive state with no pulses until PWM is fully configured and enabled, and the first active duty cycle shall be 0%.
If PWM/timer or PA8 configuration fails during initialization, the firmware shall place PA8 in a defined inactive state and shall not toggle the output.
PWM duty-cycle percentage shall be defined as the proportion of time that D7/PA8 is at logic-high level within each PWM period.
The firmware shall provide a mechanism to override the default 1 kHz PWM carrier frequency.

categories.name: PWM Ramp Control Logic
categories.description: Covers the continuous linear duty-cycle ramp sequence, timing, endpoints, direction reversal, reset behavior, saturation, and repetition.
requirements: Each PWM ramp cycle shall begin at 0% duty cycle.
The duty cycle shall ramp monotonically from 0% to 100% over 5.0 seconds.
The duty cycle shall ramp monotonically from 100% to 0% over the following 5.0 seconds.
A complete rise-and-fall PWM duty-cycle cycle shall be 10.0 seconds in duration.
The 10-second PWM duty-cycle ramp cycle shall repeat continuously until reset or power-off.
After reset, the firmware shall restart the PWM sequence from the defined initial state (0% duty cycle).
The PWM duty-cycle ramp shall be linear.
The duty-cycle endpoints shall be 0% and 100%.
The firmware shall saturate the computed PWM duty cycle to the inclusive range 0% to 100% before applying it to the output.
At both duty-cycle endpoints (0% and 100%), the firmware shall reverse the ramp direction immediately with no intentional hold time.

categories.name: Nonblocking Waveform Update Execution
categories.description: Covers duty-cycle update scheduling and resolution needed to maintain normal firmware execution while producing a smooth PWM ramp.
requirements: The firmware shall avoid blocking delays that prevent normal firmware execution during duty-cycle updates.
Duty-cycle increment steps shall be sufficiently small to produce a smooth ramp without perceptible jumps or long pauses.

categories.name: External Load and USB Development Interface
categories.description: Covers safe interfacing of loads beyond MCU GPIO limits and USB-based board power, programming, and debugging.
requirements: High-power loads shall not be connected directly to the MCU pin; an external driver stage shall be used when controlling loads that exceed GPIO electrical limits.
A USB connection shall be used for board power, programming, and debugging during development and verification.
